newsitem.title: USA: EPA seeks fine against Cook Inlet Pipeline Co.
newsitem.headline: EPA seeks fine against Cook Inlet Pipeline Co.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said on Tuesday it will seek $120,000 in penalties for water-pollution violations committed by Cook Inlet Pipeline Co.

The company, a consortium owned by Unocal, Atlantic Richfield, Mobil and Marathon at the time of the violations, operates the Drift River oil terminal on the west side of Alaska's Cook Inlet. Marathon is no longer a member of the Cook Inlet Pipeline consortium, EPA said.

According to the EPA's administrative complaint, filed by the agency's Northwest regional office, Cook Inlet Pipeline had discharges that violated the Clean Water Act 35 times between August 1992 and August 1996.
Cook Inlet was not immediately available to comment.

The discharges polluted Alaska's Redoubt Bay with oil, grease and other wastes, the complaint said. Redoubt Bay is an important salmon habitat used extensively by commercial and sport fishermen, EPA said.
The Drift River terminal is used to collect oil from Cook Inlet drilling platforms. Oil collected at the terminal is loaded into tankers travelling Cook Inlet.
